title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a stencilled (duplicated) typescript, page '- 10 -', reproduced upside down. It is almost certainly the back of a reused sheet: the surrounding manuscript pages are about F-crystals with multiplication by an order o and the trivialisation of ξ_p, a topic unrelated to this page. The typescript is part of an elementary text on analytic (holomorphic) functions of several variables over a valued field K (probably R or C). There, 'holomorphic' means locally the sum of a convergent power series, possibly with values in a Banach space.

The page opens with the end of a statement: a convergent power series has a holomorphic sum in its polycylinder of convergence.

Proposition 6 states that composites of holomorphic maps are holomorphic. It is deduced from the corollary of an earlier 'th. 2', presumably on substituting power series into power series.

Proposition 6 bis states that if [z_1...z_r] is a continuous multilinear map E_1×...×E_r → F of Banach spaces and f_i are holomorphic with values in E_i, then [f_1...f_r] is holomorphic. The proof is given for r=2. Products of absolutely summable families under a bounded bilinear map are absolutely summable, because ||[z_1.z_2]|| ≤ k||z_1||·||z_2||. This is applied to the local power-series expansions of f_1 and f_2.

The corollary says a K^q-valued map is holomorphic if and only if each component is. This is standard foundational material, of the kind found in Bourbaki's Variétés différentielles et analytiques (fascicule de résultats) or in course notes on analytic functions. It serves only as basic foundations for analytic functions.
errors: No mathematical errors. The proof of 6 bis is a sketch. One also needs the double family [x_λ.y_μ] to regroup into a power series in the variables, which follows from absolute summability.
